description: A parent feeds their baby two flavors of baby food, apple and carrot, in order to meet the babies fat and folate requirements. Each serving of apple flavored baby food contains 2 units of fat and 5 units of folate. Each serving of carrot flavored baby food contains 4 units of fat and 3 units of folate. The baby does not like the carrot flavor, and therefore he must eat three times as many apple flavored baby food as carrot flavored baby food. However, he must eat at least 2 servings of carrot flavored baby food. If the baby can consume at most 100 units of folate, how many servings of each should he eat to maximize his fat intake?

FatApple.definition: Fat units per serving of apple flavored baby food

FolateApple.definition: Folate units per serving of apple flavored baby food

FatCarrot.definition: Fat units per serving of carrot flavored baby food

FolateCarrot.definition: Folate units per serving of carrot flavored baby food

AppleToCarrotRatio.definition: Multiplier for the number of apple servings relative to carrot servings

MinCarrotServings.definition: Minimum servings of carrot flavored baby food

objective.description: "The goal is to maximize the baby's total fat intake from apple and carrot flavored baby food servings."

AppleServings.definition: Number of servings of apple flavored baby food

CarrotServings.definition: Number of servings of carrot flavored baby food
